text:
- [LSCO.4.5.9] **Assertion and retraction.** Facts are schema-typed; assertion is
  through `emit`; retraction is via TTL,
  meaningful-change, `logical` justifier-end, or `withdraw`.

  **A rule retracts a fact only by `withdraw`, and only one it matched:**

  - A rule that matches fact X and removes X in its RHS creates the same
    oscillation risk as a rule that emits X — the removal of X can let
    the rule fire again, re-establishing the very condition that
    triggers it. `[LCYC.3.1.1]` admits exactly the shapes that cannot:
    a rule that only matches and withdraws X, never also emits it
    within the same cycle. A rule pair that matches this clause's own
    oscillation risk — one rule re-emitting what another withdraws,
    in one cycle — remains rejected under `[LCYC.3.1.1]`, not merely
    warned about.
  - Retraction in rules violates the declarative model unless it is
    consumption: `withdraw` acts only on a binding the rule itself
    matched, stating "the fact I read is now spent," not an arbitrary
    imperative delete. Rules that do not consume stay idempotent and
    order-independent; `withdraw` creates execution-order dependence
    only where a rule's own semantics already are order-dependent (it
    consumed something).
  - The sanctioned retraction mechanisms:
      1. **TTL expiry** — size the schema's `ttl` to the
         desired lifetime. The engine retracts when the
         deadline passes.
      2. **Meaningful-change / tolerance dedup** — an
         identical (or within-tolerance) reassertion is a
         no-op; the existing fact is not replaced.
      3. **Truth-maintenance on `emit X logical`**
         — the engine retracts X when the LHS patterns
         that justified it are no longer matched ([LLOG.15.1]).
         This is the `logical` schema retraction path.
      4. **`withdraw <binding>`, `scope explicit` or `internal`
         only** ([LSCP.2.6.1]) — a rule consumes a fact it matched. Admitted only where
         `[LCYC.3.1.1]`'s certificate accepts the resulting rule
         graph. A binding of any other scope is a compile refusal,
         `DS_VALIDATE_WITHDRAW_SCOPE`: `[LLOG.11.8]` for `logical`;
         `activation` and `ambient` are engine-managed and
         author-read-only respectively, neither an author's to end.

idris.name: lsco_4_5_9__refill_drain_diverges
idris.note: Executed and checked: period 2 from the start. The removal of X lets refill fire again, re-establishing the condition drain fires on -- the clause's stated risk, exhibited on the deterministic engine. What the [LCYC] amendment's certificate refuses: X is emitted, read and withdrawn in one SCC.

idris.name: lsco_4_5_9__drain
idris.note: `X x -> withdraw x`: the fourth sanctioned mechanism, as an action -- admitted alone, and in any SCC where nothing also emits X.

idris.name: lsco_4_5_9__refill
idris.note: `no X -> emit X`: the rule the clause's oscillation re-arms.

idris.name: lsco_4_5_9__refill_drain
idris.note: The pair, over an explicit kind, refill first.
